headline: Strongest near-compact root lead found: Xiaomi 17 Pro. Its retail unlock path is still unverified.
summary: The 112 inventory entries cover 20 Android brands; they establish market breadth, not 112 independently verified root successes. Xiaomi 17 Pro has an explicit owner report of root after multiple reboots on a named build. It is a candidate to investigate, not a guarantee that a newly purchased locked unit can reach that state.
lead_order: Xiaomi 18 Pro — China shipping; global not yet shipping
OPPO Find X9s Pro — China compact

takeaways.title: Investigate Xiaomi 17 Pro first if a small size overrun is acceptable
takeaways.detail: China 25098PN5AC / pandora: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, 6,300 mAh and 192 g; 151.1 × 71.8 mm is 1.5 mm taller and 0.3 mm wider than iPhone 16 Pro. An owner reports KernelSU Next working after multiple reboots on xiaomi.eu OS3.0.318.0.WBLCNXM. Initial unlocking from the exact retail stock build remains unverified. It launched in September 2025, not 2026.

takeaways.title: Newer compact hardware deserves a place, but not an invented root guarantee
takeaways.detail: OnePlus 15T, OPPO Find X9s Pro, vivo X300 FE/X500 Pro, Honor Magic8 Pro Air/Magic9 and Xiaomi 18 Pro are all relevant hardware alternatives. Evidence varies from owner/project reports to temporary root, a secondary-reported researcher demonstration, or no corroborated success. A newer temporary-root result does not prove or disprove an older build's different method.

takeaways.title: For a literal height-and-width limit, Galaxy S25 is the recent flagship fallback
takeaways.detail: Galaxy S25 is 146.9 × 70.5 mm and 162 g, with owner-rooted international-build reports. Its 4,000 mAh battery and 2025 Snapdragon 8 Elite are compromises against newer large-battery candidates. Already-unlocked or older-build success is not proof that a sealed phone on current One UI can be unlocked. The strict-size filter also includes older fallbacks, so check release dates.

coverage_note: Scope: principally 2025–2026 non-folding flagship and plausible compact devices, with a few explicitly aged or midrange fallbacks to explain exclusions. Regional variants and oversized family representatives are separate where their evidence differs; rows are not a count of unique phone designs. Announced-but-not-shipping products remain labeled. This is a broad practical inventory, not an exhaustive list of every Android ever sold.
coverage_gaps: Missing public owner proof is labeled unverified, not unrootable. Exact retail SKUs, full successful firmware and current OTA compatibility remain incomplete for many new models; seller packages and generic guides are not treated as owner success.

Temporary root is explicitly separated from reboot-persistent root. Some ordinary rooted-owner reports lack a controlled reboot transcript; the evidence panel states what was actually reported. Maintained ROM/kernel support does not guarantee that every locked retail unit can be unlocked.

Regional batteries differ materially on Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO, Honor, Nothing and RedMagic. Compare independent runtimes only within the same test and tested regional hardware; do not rank GSMArena, PCMark, video-loop and web-browsing hours as one scale.

Recent-family gaps remain explicit: vanilla Xiaomi 18 was not shipping; vivo X500 FE was certification-only; some proposed mini/Air models were unverified or canceled. Huawei Pura 90 Pro was separately screened out for size and its HarmonyOS-platform detour; HMD Skyline is older midrange hardware. No brand-wide impossibility claim is made.

Rooted phones can lose banking, payments or employer-device compatibility. The Xiaomi 17 Pro source itself documents Intune rejecting the rooted phone. Singapore bands/VoLTE, warranty and actual daily apps need checking on the intended unit. No security-policy or DRM bypass is proposed.

devices.unlock_root_evidence: June 2026: owner Oosl identifies OnePlus 15T / 16.0.8.300 and reports installing KernelSU, updating and rebooting; the boot warning was gone afterward. This is a first-hand rooted-setup/reboot report, not a controlled post-reboot privilege check; initial unlock and any boot intervention are undocumented. Separately, the maintained LineageOS fairlady installation guide names exact model PLZ110 and an Android 16 stock prerequisite: real device-specific ROM/unlock support, not an owner unlock transcript or a guarantee every retail unit qualifies. October 2026: the exact ColorOS 17 project below reports uid=0 and SELinux Enforcing, but explicitly loses root after reboot. That newer TEMP_ROOT_ONLY method neither disproves the older owner report nor proves its compatibility with newer firmware.
devices.firmware: June owner: 16.0.8.300; full regional suffix, kernel and security patch unspecified. Project/module 5.3.120 is not the handset firmware. Other separate GhostLock claim: ColorOS 16.0.9.400 / kernel 6.12.38.

Confirm a current successful LineageOS installation and compatible firmware.
